newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: W.Australia calls for petrochemical plant interest.
newsitem.headline: W.Australia calls for petrochemical plant interest.

text.p: The Western Australian state government will call for expressions of interest in developing a A$1 billion world-scale petrochemical plant to be known as the Pilbara Petrochemical Project, state Resouces Minister Colin Barnett said on Friday.

Barnett said state cabinet had approved the next step in the development process after significant studies into the competitiveness of a plant in the Pilbara region and associated infrastructure requirements.
"The government has identified the development of a privately-funded petrochemical plant as the major resource development opportunity in Western Australia this decade," he said in a statement.
"I am very confident the project will proceed and that it will be under construction by the turn of this century. It will be a major milestone for resource development in W.A.," he said.
The Pilbara petrochemical project would be based on ethane and/or LPG contained in natural gas coming onshore from the North-West Shelf.

The state government said in February this year that at least five overseas companies, including Dow Chemical Co and Imperial Chemical Industries Plc, had expressed interest in participating in a petrochemical project in the state.
